lines: RESEARCH ARTICLE
SiT Dataset: Socially Interactive Pedestrian Trajectory Dataset for Social
Navigation Robots
Source figure: p. 7
QUESTION / P. 2
How can we capture interactive behaviors between
pedestrians and a mobile robot in the real world using
pedestrian trajectories?
METHOD / P. 3
SiT used a mobile robot to record indoor and outdoor scenes
with two 3D scanning LiDARs, five cameras covering a
360-degree view, two inertial measurement units (IMUs), and
real-time kinematic positioning (RTK). Each scene spans 20
seconds at 10 Hz.
KEY FINDING / P. 7
The SiT dataset captured more instances of a robot and pedestrian sharing
the same semantic space while within 2 meters of each other than the other
three autonomous driving datasets (Waymo Open, Argoverse2, and
nuScenes).
Figure 8: Comparison with other autonomous vehicle datasets. (a) represents the normalized density graph of the
distance between the robot (or ego-vehicle) and surrounding pedestrians, while (b) illustrates the number of
instances that satisfy some criteria. Space sharing condition refers to instances where the robot and pedestrians
occupy the same semantic space, Proximity condition indicates cases where the distance between the robot and
pedestrian is within 2 meters, and Sharing & Proxi. indicates cases that fulfill both conditions.
